declared_readings: Key: ContentDigest, algorithm and digest, compared exactly with no case folding. The digest identifies the bytes; the manifest handle is caller-owned and may differ between clips of one file; asset_id is optional. Limit: identical bytes imported twice are one media item.

Studio-minted, not in the spec: schema id hsk.studio.media_markers@1, token media_markers, command ids media_marker.add, .replace, .remove, codes invalid_digest, invalid_marker, duplicate_marker, marker_missing, and every Rust and wire name beyond the clause, including AppearingMarker, ClipMarkers, SequenceMarkers, ClipMediaItem, clip_appearing_markers, sequence_appearing_markers.

Limits, Studio bounds: MAX_MEDIA_MARKER_ITEMS 4096, MAX_MEDIA_MARKERS 65536 (the per-sequence marker bound) over all items, MAX_MEDIA_MARKER_INPUT_BYTES 16 MiB whatever the budget allows; items and markers together charge Budget::nodes, their text Budget::payload_bytes. At the default budget that is 4096 nodes and 1 MiB.

An item with no marker has no entry. A stored entry with an empty marker list is refused InvalidField, so one state has one form; removing the last marker removes the item, and the last item removes the document entry.

One marker id space over three scopes. validate_document checks sequence and clip markers; the records check extends it to this scope. A commit or resync that gives a document marker an id a valid entry holds is refused folio_rejected, as the settings guard refuses. This is the entry's only hold on a document edit. An entry already invalid does not hold a commit up. An undo or redo landing on an id taken since is refused too.
One records step can move a marker between scopes, the id space being checked at the end of the step.
An item no clip is cut from is valid; no read lists such items.

Item 4, run green in the bundled run at 4ffe1b06. Mapping: playback's, source_to_timeline for speed and reverse, the half-open window, rounding toward the clip start. SUPERSEDED by F-R57-1: a reversed point appears where frame_layers shows its frame, never on the exclusive end (notes.remediation_R57).

Item 4, run green in the bundled run at 4ffe1b06. Frame hold: a held clip plays one source tick, so a marker holding it spans the whole clip and any other is hidden, for the clip's own markers too. Exact tick match, no frame grid, so a marker inside the held frame past its first tick is hidden. A held frame outside the window still counts, as playback shows it. Vendor parity UNVERIFIED (D5).

Item 4, run green in the bundled run at 4ffe1b06. A disabled clip still shows markers. A nested sequence or primitive source has no media item, ClipMediaItem says so, and inner clips' markers are not lifted to the outer clip. Hidden is a counter, summed per clip in a sequence read. More than MAX_MARKERS_PER_SEQUENCE appearing is limit_exceeded, never truncated. SUPERSEDED by F-R57-15: a sequence read charges MAX_APPEARING_WALK before it maps a marker, and is cancellable.

R56 F-R56-7, from origin, now applies to this entry: records that do not validate against the document the undo restores cannot go back, the half is dropped and the step says so. Before the rebase this lane's undo was handed out and then refused.

R57. A zero-length marker on a reversed clip belongs to a frame: every tick of that frame maps to one timeline tick, where the picture's position law reaches the frame's start, rounded toward the clip start. On a window too short to reach it, the clip's last tick. Vendor parity UNVERIFIED (D5).

R57. "First displayed tick" is the position law's tick for the frame. frame_sampling's nearest rule also shows that frame up to half a frame earlier off the sequence's frame ticks; those ticks are not where a sequence frame starts, and forward speeds map the same way.

R57. MAX_APPEARING_WALK = 2^24, Studio's bound: 256 clips of an item holding the 65536 markers a record set may hold. A larger valid file gets limit_exceeded from the sequence read; clip_appearing_markers walks one clip, linear in its input, and is not charged.
